dublinCore.dc:title: 116 HR 7064 IH: Stop Funding the PLA Act
dublinCore.dc:rights: Pursuant to Title 17 Section 105 of the United States Code, this file is not subject to copyright protection and is in the public domain.

action.action-desc: Mr. Banks (for himself, Mr. Gallagher, and Mr. LaMalfa) introduced the following bill; which was referred to the Committee on Financial Services, and in addition to the Committee on Foreign Affairs, for a period to be subsequently determined by the Speaker, in each case for consideration of such provisions as fall within the jurisdiction of the committee concerned

form.official-title: To prohibit financial investment by a United States person in foreign industrial defense corporations with substantial contracts with, ties to, or support from, the Chinese military and affiliated entities, and for other purposes.

section.text: This Act may be cited as the Stop Funding the PLA Act.

section.header: Specification of prohibited foreign industrial defense corporations

subsection.text: Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this section, and annually thereafter, the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the domestic intelligence community, shall submit to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives a report that specifies each foreign industrial defense corporation with substantial contracts with, ties to, or support from, a PLA entity.

paragraph.text: Beginning on the date that is 180 days after a report is submitted under subsection (a), a United States person may not purchase securities of a foreign industrial defense corporation specified in such report.

subparagraph.text: Except as provided in subparagraph (B), not later than 180 days after a report is submitted under subsection (a), a United States person that owns a security of a foreign industrial defense corporation specified in such report shall divest themselves of such security.

subparagraph.header: Extended wind-down in case of financial hardship
subparagraph.text: The Secretary may allow a United States person a 270-day extension to the 180-day period for compliance under subparagraph (A) if the Secretary determines that such entity—

clause.text: owns a security of a foreign industrial defense corporation specified in a report submitted under subsection (a); and
would experience extreme financial hardship to comply within the 180-day period under subparagraph (A).

paragraph.text: The Secretary shall enforce the provisions of this section.
Not later than 90 days after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary shall issue such regulations and guidance as necessary to implement and enforce this section.

subsection.text: Not later than 360 days after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives a report on the progress of the divestments required under subsection (b)(2).

paragraph.text: A foreign industrial defense corporation may petition the Secretary to not be included or removed from a report under subsection (a).

A petition under paragraph (1) shall include such documentation of the assets and liabilities, company financial records, ownership and investor records, and past and current business contracts of the foreign industrial defense corporation submitting such petition that the Secretary determines necessary.

subsection.text: Not later than 8 years after the date of the enactment of this section, the Secretary shall submit to the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs of the Senate and the Committee on Financial Services of the House of Representatives a final report on the implementation of this section, including—

paragraph.text: an analysis of the effectiveness of this section;
the development and maintenance of the reports required under subsection (a); and
a description of completed and ongoing civil and criminal cases related to securities of foreign industrial defense corporations.

subsection.text: This section and the authority under this section shall expire on the date that is 10 years after the date of the enactment of this section.

paragraph.text: The term PLA entity means any entity of the Chinese military, including the People’s Liberation Army, Navy, Air Force, Rocket Force, Strategic Support Force, and Joint Logistics Force, and the Chinese intelligence community.
The term foreign industrial defense corporation means any corporation based—

subparagraph.text: outside of the United States; and

in a country that the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of Defense, the Secretary of State, and the domestic intelligence community, determines does not possess positive economic and military relations with the United States.

paragraph.text: The term Secretary means the Secretary of the Treasury.

The term substantial shall, with respect to contracts with, ties to, or support from, a PLA entity, have the meaning determined by the Secretary, in consultation with the Secretary of State, the Secretary of Defense, and the domestic intelligence community.
